To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Inhibitors of the PI3/Akt/mTOR pathway are active against acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cells, but the combination of PI3K/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) dual inhibitors is more effective than inhibitors of PI3/Akt or mTOR alone.
Dual PI3K-mTOR inhibitors profoundly inhibit growth and survival of all ALL cells irrespective of BCR-ABL expression and responsiveness to ABL TKI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of drugs that target the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway.
the development and characterization of novel inhibitors of the PI3-kinase/AKT/mTOR pathway and their use for treatment of leukemia.
the development of novel targeted therapeutics for the treatment of patients with ALL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dual PI3K and TOR inhibition is superior to PI3K or TOR inhibition alone.
dual inhibition of the PI3k/mTORC1/2 pathway may be a promising approach in ALL, but further research is required to establish its clinical benefit.

dual PI3K and TORC1 inhibitors are promising therapeutic approaches for patients with ALL, and that greater antileukemia activity of dual inhibitors is probably related to the redundant function between PI3K and the TORC1 complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway is an attractive therapeutic strategy in B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), and that dual inhibitors of PI3k/mTOR1/C2 are promising agents for this purpose.
the PI3K and/or mTOR pathway is an important target in ALL.
PI3K/mTor inhibitors are promising therapeutic agents for ALL and the most potent inhibitors would be dual inhibitors targeting both mTorC1 and mTorC2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PI3K-mTOR signaling pathway is a critical survival pathway in ALL and that inhibition of this pathway is a promising approach in ALL.
inhibition of the PI3k/AKT/mTORC1 pathway is a promising approach for treating patients with ALL, regardless of whether their leukemia cells have the BCR-AB1 oncoprotein or not.
the PI3K and AKT pathways are essential for survival of BCR-ABL and TEL-ABL positive ALL cells.
